entries.definition: A neural next-word architecture that factors word probabilities along a binary vocabulary tree and shares a nonlinear branch predictor conditioned on context-word embeddings and a separate embedding of the current tree node.
entries.identity_notes: This record covers Morin and Bengio’s 2005 shared-predictor architecture, including its WordNet-guided tree construction. It is a complete language model, distinct from the generic hierarchical-softmax output component and from HLBL’s linear context representation with node-vector scores. The title is scoped to this original construction, not every probabilistic language model using a hierarchy. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 355 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared, with no normalized identity match. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in both worktree and main, returning 54 lines each. None is an existing record for these complete architectures. Twenty exact AIO nodes and their generated records plus four complete native neighbors were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Target evaluation work scales with path length and the branch-predictor cost. A logarithmic path requires suitable tree depth; producing the entire vocabulary distribution still requires at least linear output work.
The learned tree distribution is exactly normalized for its own parameters, but is not an equality-preserving numerical shortcut for a previously specified flat-softmax network.

Choosing one frequent WordNet sense loses other senses. Multiple leaves per word are discussed as an extension and require summed path probabilities; this record does not attribute that implementation to the original experiment.
Shared parameters reduce independent per-node parameterization but do not make the hidden activities identical at all nodes or establish convex learning or global convergence.

The accessed reissue PDF has unresolved references and a page-count discrepancy against its landing-page pagination; evidence is tied to the exact six-page file. No claimed speedup, test ranking or author-code behavior is certified.

claims.statement: Concatenate the embeddings of the preceding context words into x, sharing their embedding matrix across all tree nodes. For internal node n, compute q_n=sigmoid(alpha_n+beta^T tanh(c+W x+U N_n)), where N_n is its separately learned node embedding, alpha_n is its scalar bias, and beta, c, W and U are shared parameters. The binary code for a target word chooses q_n or 1-q_n at each node; multiply those factors to obtain its normalized next-word probability. Training backpropagates the observed-word log loss through nodes on that path and their shared parameters. Although W x can be reused, tanh(c+W x+U N_n) generally differs by node. The reported tree starts from WordNet, selects one parent for multiply parented nodes and the most frequent sense per word, then makes nonbinary branches binary using corpus-based clustering. This hierarchy is a modeling choice, not a semantic-equivalence guarantee.

entries.name: Log-bilinear language model
entries.definition: A next-word language architecture that linearly combines position-specific transforms of context-word embeddings and normalizes their bilinear compatibility with candidate-word embeddings over the vocabulary.
entries.identity_notes: This is the original Mnih–Hinton LBL construction. It uses the same word-embedding matrix for context and candidate words, has no stochastic hidden variables, and retains a flat vocabulary normalizer. HLBL replaces that output parameterization with tree-node decisions. The FRBM and temporal FRBM in the same 2007 paper are separate latent-variable architectures, not aliases for LBL. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 355 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared, with no normalized identity match. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in both worktree and main, returning 54 lines each. All 41 unique matched contents were read: source references, complete-model contrasts, frontier leads and prior review context for the hierarchical-softmax component. None is an existing record for these complete architectures. Twenty exact AIO nodes and their generated records plus four complete native neighbors were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The context feature computation is linear, while normalization makes word probabilities nonlinear. Position-specific transforms preserve context order; the construction is not generally a bag-of-words model.

Without an additional exact computational method, the original flat normalizer requires summing candidate scores over the vocabulary. Absence of stochastic hidden variables makes this expectation explicit, not independent of vocabulary size.

Bilinear scores and shared learned embeddings do not make joint parameter fitting a convex optimization problem. Exact likelihood gradients do not guarantee a global optimum or calibrated predictions.
The energy scores one candidate conditional on its context; it is not the unnormalized energy of a whole sequence used by the pinned ImplicitLanguageModel or EnergyBasedLLM classes.
The record covers a fixed-context word model, without asserting long-context capability, benchmark superiority, author-code behavior or the mechanisms of the neighboring FRBM variants.

claims.statement: In the 2007 row-vector convention, let r_w be a word’s embedding written as a column, C_i the transform for context position i, b_r a feature bias and b_w a candidate-word bias. The candidate score is sum_i r_context_i^T C_i r_w+b_r^T r_w+b_w. Equivalently, form r_hat=b_r+sum_i C_i^T r_context_i once, then take score_w=r_hat^T r_w+b_w and apply the vocabulary softmax. The original energy is the negative of this score. Maximum-likelihood gradients are observed sufficient statistics minus their exact finite-vocabulary conditional expectations. Because the embedding matrix is shared, its gradient includes both input-context and candidate-output roles. The 2008 exposition writes r_hat=sum_i C_i r_context_i with the opposite matrix orientation and without an explicit feature bias; this is a notation/parameterization distinction to preserve when comparing formulas.

entries.definition: A next-word language architecture that computes one linear context feature vector and uses its dot products with internal-node vectors to assign normalized vocabulary-tree probabilities, summing path probabilities when a word has multiple codes.
entries.identity_notes: This is Mnih and Hinton’s 2008 HLBL architecture, not a synonym for every hierarchical language model or the hierarchical-softmax component. It combines a position-weighted linear context representation with learned node vectors. Flat LBL, Morin–Bengio’s node-conditioned nonlinear network, and the tree-building algorithm each have distinct scopes. One-code and multiple-code forms are explicitly part of the source’s model family. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 355 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared, with no normalized identity match. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in both worktree and main, returning 54 lines each. All 41 unique matched contents were read: source references, complete-model contrasts, frontier leads and prior review context for the hierarchical-softmax component. None is an existing record for these complete architectures. Twenty exact AIO nodes and their generated records plus four complete native neighbors were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The linear context feature is reusable across nodes; it does not include Morin–Bengio’s node-dependent tanh hidden computation. A diagonal transform is a restriction on the model parameters, not a requirement for the general probability construction.
The tree defines its own normalized distribution and need not reproduce flat-LBL probabilities for matching-looking parameters. Tree choice and finite context constrain the representation.

Target cost includes context computation plus the visited path nodes. Multiple codes require their summed probability and increase work; a general adaptive or full binary tree need not have logarithmic worst-case depth. Reporting every word probability requires at least linear output work.

Multiple codes need not represent distinct senses. The source’s discussion reports that replicated words were often rare or difficult to cluster and notes that averaging their contexts can lose multimodal usage structure.

The paper’s mean-code-length statistic sums lengths over all codes of a word before frequency weighting; treating it as the mean of that word’s code lengths would understate its reported evaluation work.

No universal semantic clustering quality, speedup, predictive advantage, convergence guarantee or author implementation behavior is asserted. The tree-building procedure is described as architectural context, not separately curated as an equivalent model.

claims.statement: Using the 2008 column-vector convention, form r_hat=sum_i C_i r_context_i once for the preceding words. At internal node j, assign left-branch probability sigmoid(r_hat^T q_j+b_j) and use its complement for the right branch. Multiply the decisions along a leaf code. With one leaf per word this is its probability; with multiple codes, sum all disjoint leaf probabilities assigned to that word. Optimize the penalized observed-word log likelihood. For multiple codes, differentiating the log of that sum weights each path gradient by its posterior share of the word’s probability; choosing one path or averaging their log losses is a different objective. The paper uses diagonal C_i to reduce context-transformation cost. Its data-driven trees bootstrap features from a random-tree model and represent each word by the mean predicted context feature at its occurrences before recursive clustering; balanced, adaptive and multiple-code tree policies are distinct choices.

mapping_assessment: All 85 semantic label/scoped-synonym hits were read, followed by 20 complete CLASS nodes with annotations/outgoing edges and corresponding generated YAML, and four complete native neighbors. All three architectures broadly map to AutoregressiveLanguageModel: they model next words from preceding finite context. This uses sequential factorization, not the AIO definition’s qualitative performance claim. LanguageModel is also broader but redundant. HierarchicalLanguageModel describes multilevel language representations rather than uniquely identifying a word-probability tree. ImplicitLanguageModel and EnergyBasedLLM score whole sequences without autoregressive factorization, unlike LBL’s conditional energy. FactoredLanguageModel denotes explicit linguistic factors; FactorizedLLM denotes component/expert decomposition. DeepFeedForwardNetwork inherits the multiple-hidden-layer requirement, while the named constructions do not require that depth; Perceptron is a binary linear classifier. EmbeddingLayer, OutputLayer, SoftmaxLayer, HiddenLayer and ProbabilisticHiddenLayer are components, not equivalent complete architectures. BayesianNetwork provides a broader factorization viewpoint but not these parameterizations. RBM/Boltzmann identities require stochastic undirected structure absent here. HierarchicalSoftmax is an output component; DocNADE has additive order-insensitive prefix features, NADE binary fully visible conditionals, and ReplicatedSoftmax undirected length-conditioned latent structure. These older records are boundary context, not newly approved targets.

native_neighbors.name: Hierarchical softmax
native_neighbors.definition: A neural categorical-output component that assigns a probability to each vocabulary leaf by multiplying normalized branch probabilities along its path through a word tree.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record covers the hierarchical probability output component, including the binary sigmoid form described as hierarchical softmax by Mikolov and colleagues. Morin and Bengio’s parameter-sharing language model and Mnih and Hinton’s hierarchical log-bilinear model are complete architectures using this factorization, not aliases for the component. A Huffman tree, a WordNet-derived tree and a learned tree are construction choices with different scope. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 352 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared, with no normalized identity match. Both full-checkout searches included ignored and hidden files; worktree returned 15 lines and main 19. All 16 unique matched contents were read: DocNADE contrasts, frontier and review references, plus four ignored-environment Sage/Pygments entries unrelated to AI SAGE. Twenty-one exact AIO nodes and four complete native neighbors were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The tree parameterization defines a normalized distribution of its own. Calling it an approximation to full softmax does not assert equality to probabilities from a particular flat-softmax parameter set or provide a numerical approximation-error bound.

Logarithmic target cost requires suitable depth or weighted-average code length. A full binary tree alone can have linear worst-case depth. Even a Huffman code’s mean length need not be at most log2(vocabulary size): three equally frequent words have optimal mean length 5/3, exceeding log2(3). Thus the unqualified average-length sentence in Mikolov Section 2.1 is not adopted as a universal bound.
Computing every vocabulary probability requires at least linear output work. The short-path calculation does not by itself give a logarithmic-time exact top-k or most-probable-word search.

Shared internal nodes, tree construction and input representation constrain the fitted model. Multiple codes per word add paths and require their sum, rather than selecting an arbitrary single leaf or averaging leaf probabilities.

This component is not a whole language model, a hard decision tree, negative sampling, or Gumbel-Softmax sampling. No empirical speedup, embedding-quality ranking or author-code behavior is certified.

claims.statement: In a binary tree with one leaf per word, each internal node computes a branch probability from the input representation, commonly sigmoid of a node-vector dot product with optional bias. The opposite branch has its complement. Multiply the appropriate branch probabilities on the target word’s path to obtain its exact probability under this tree-parameterized distribution; probabilities over all leaves sum to one. The negative log probability is a sum of binary losses, so only nodes on the observed path contribute output-parameter gradients. For a sigmoid node logit and branch indicator y, that loss derivative is sigmoid(logit)-y. Computing one target probability and its gradient costs work proportional to its path length, in addition to representation computation. The source’s skip-gram variant uses internal-node output vectors and frequency-based Huffman codes. Multiple leaves assigned to one word require summing their disjoint path probabilities, as in the HLBL extension.

native_neighbors.name: Document NADE
native_neighbors.definition: A neural autoregressive document model that predicts successive words from shared additive embeddings of the preceding words, using normalized word conditionals and a deterministic document representation.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This is Larochelle and Lauly’s original Document NADE. The final construction uses binary-tree word probabilities, with a flat-softmax intermediate derivation. It is inspired by Replicated Softmax but is a separately normalized directed model with deterministic hidden features, not the same undirected latent-variable model. Its full-document representation is invariant to word permutation, while its unsymmetrized sequence probability need not be. Supervised and distributional-prior extensions require separate scope decisions. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 349 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 5 and 5 lines respectively. All 3 unique matched line contents were inspected in full: the prior NADE-variant lead, RNADE source URL and previous review exclusion, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Seventeen exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and five full native neighboring records were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Order invariance of the summed document representation does not imply exchangeability of the sequence likelihood. The symmetrized probability of each sequence differs from its count-vector probability by the number of distinct permutations; duplicate words change that number.

For a word whose tree path has length L, conditional output work is O(HL). The claimed logarithmic vocabulary scaling requires suitable tree depth or average depth; a full binary tree alone can have linear depth. The record does not assert a logarithmic worst case for every full tree.

The main paper’s text below Equation (11) retains vi=1 in the joint product although words are categorical. The curated likelihood uses the observed word and its branch path, consistent with Equations (9) and (11) and the supplement’s probability computation.

For Bernoulli tree training, the negative-log-likelihood derivative is the probability of the right branch minus the observed branch indicator. The supplement’s p(actual branch)-indicator notation must not be read literally as the probability of the observed left branch when that indicator is zero. No author implementation behavior is inferred.

The stated model is conditional on document length and does not supply a learned document-length distribution. Shared additive prefix features discard order within the observed prefix. Hidden topic features are deterministic representations, not posterior latent-topic probabilities.
No classification/retrieval advantage, semantic quality guarantee, exact symmetrized-mixture training gradient or implementation certification is asserted.

claims.statement: For a document of given length D, form h_i=sigmoid(c+sum_(k<i) W[:,v_k]); the same word embedding and output parameters are reused across positions, and the preactivation is updated by adding the newly observed word’s embedding. A flat softmax can normalize the next-word distribution. The paper’s final model replaces it with a binary tree whose leaves are vocabulary words: each internal node predicts the probability of taking its right branch, and a word probability is the product of its observed left/right branch probabilities. Multiply all observed-word conditionals to obtain a normalized probability over length-D sequences. Train by differentiating their negative log likelihood. After all words, h(v)=sigmoid(c+sum_i W[:,v_i]) is an order-invariant document representation; tanh is also tested. For count-vector input, the paper samples word occurrences without replacement to produce uniformly random distinct orderings and trains on those sequences. Its separate symmetrized sequence model averages probabilities over distinct permutations; training on sampled order log losses is a surrogate for that log mixture. A count-vector probability instead sums the unsymmetrized sequence probabilities over its distinct permutations.

native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record covers the original binary NADE construction of Larochelle and Murray. Its neural hidden activations are deterministic functions of the visible prefix, not stochastic latent variables to be summed out. Mean-field RBM calculations motivate the parameterization; NADE is a separately normalized directed model and does not require a pretrained RBM. Later order-agnostic, real-valued, document and conditional variants need their own scope assessments. The inspected publisher PDF contains inconsistent executable-looking notation: Algorithm 1 initializes a multiplicatively updated probability to zero and places a plus between the two Bernoulli factors; the displayed accumulator-difference equation on printed p.31 uses i+1 where the prefix difference requires i. claims.statement: Fix an ordering of D binary observations. For each position i compute h_i=sigmoid(c+W[:,<i] x_<i) and r_i=P(x_i=1|x_<i)=sigmoid(b_i+V[i,:] h_i). The original motivation ties V to the transpose of W, while the paper explicitly also learns separate output weights V; sharing W and c across positions is retained. The joint probability is the product over i of r_i raised to x_i times (1-r_i) raised to (1-x_i). Initialize the hidden preactivation accumulator a_1=c and update a_(i+1)=a_i+W[:,i] x_i after evaluating position i. This reuses prefix work and supports O(DH) evaluation for the original one-hidden-layer construction with H hidden units. Train by differentiating the exact average negative log joint probability. Generate by sampling each visible bit from its prefix conditional in order; no stochastic hidden-state inference or RBM partition function is needed for these operations.

native_neighbors.definition: An undirected document model with binary hidden units and a length-dependent set of categorical word units that share visible-to-hidden weights, with hidden biases scaled by document length.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This is the original Replicated Softmax model of Salakhutdinov and Hinton. It specializes a restricted Boltzmann machine to word-count sufficient statistics across documents of different lengths. It is distinct from repeatedly applying the ordinary softmax function, from the expected-count Constrained Poisson update discussed in the paper, and from the directed deterministic-feature Document NADE architecture. limitations: Tractable hidden posteriors do not make the partition function or equilibrium model expectation tractable. Finite-step contrastive-divergence updates are not exact maximum-likelihood gradients; deterministic expected counts are not the same as multinomial Gibbs sampling.

The model is conditional on document length and supplies no document-length distribution. Its hidden feature vector has independent conditional Bernoulli coordinates, not topic proportions constrained to sum to one.

For ordinary counting measure on K^D ordered word assignments and F binary hidden units, the zero-weight, zero-bias partition is K^D times 2^F. The AIS discussion’s printed Z_0=2^F needs a corresponding normalized base-measure convention or visible-state factor; it is not adopted unchanged as that counting-measure partition. claims.statement: For a document with D word positions, vocabulary counts n_k and binary hidden states h_j, use energy E(V,h)=-sum_jk W_jk h_j n_k-sum_k b_k n_k-D sum_j a_j h_j. The joint probability is proportional to exp(-E) with a partition function for that length. Hidden units are conditionally independent given words, with P(h_j=1|V)=sigmoid(D a_j+sum_k W_jk n_k). Given h, positions independently draw words from softmax(b_k+sum_j W_jk h_j); equivalently, sample D word counts from the corresponding multinomial. Parameter sharing makes the ordered-word probability permutation invariant. A count-vector probability includes the number of distinct ordered realizations. Learning contrasts data and model sufficient statistics; the paper approximates the model term with finite alternating Gibbs steps initialized at data.

In a binary tree with one leaf per word, each internal node computes a branch probability from the input representation, commonly sigmoid of a node-vector dot product with optional bias. The opposite branch has its complement. Multiply the appropriate branch probabilities on the target word’s path to obtain its exact probability under this tree-parameterized distribution; probabilities over all leaves sum to one. The negative log probability is a sum of binary losses, so only nodes on the observed path contribute output-parameter gradients. For a sigmoid node logit and branch indicator y, that loss derivative is sigmoid(logit)-y. Computing one target probability and its gradient costs work proportional to its path length, in addition to representation computation. The source’s skip-gram variant uses internal-node output vectors and frequency-based Huffman codes. Multiple leaves assigned to one word require summing their disjoint path probabilities, as in the HLBL extension. Limitations: The tree parameterization defines a normalized distribution of its own. Calling it an approximation to full softmax does not assert equality to probabilities from a particular flat-softmax parameter set or provide a numerical approximation-error bound. Logarithmic target cost requires suitable depth or weighted-average code length. A full binary tree alone can have linear worst-case depth. Even a Huffman code’s mean length need not be at most log2(vocabulary size): three equally frequent words have optimal mean length 5/3, exceeding log2(3). Thus the unqualified average-length sentence in Mikolov Section 2.1 is not adopted as a universal bound. Computing every vocabulary probability requires at least linear output work. The short-path calculation does not by itself give a logarithmic-time exact top-k or most-probable-word search. Shared internal nodes, tree construction and input representation constrain the fitted model. Multiple codes per word add paths and require their sum, rather than selecting an arbitrary single leaf or averaging leaf probabilities. This component is not a whole language model, a hard decision tree, negative sampling, or Gumbel-Softmax sampling. No empirical speedup, embedding-quality ranking or author-code behavior is certified.

source_analysis.mapping_assessment: All 85 semantic label/scoped-synonym hits were read, followed by 20 complete CLASS nodes with annotations/outgoing edges and corresponding generated YAML, and four complete native neighbors. All three architectures broadly map to AutoregressiveLanguageModel: they model next words from preceding finite context. This uses sequential factorization, not the AIO definition’s qualitative performance claim. LanguageModel is also broader but redundant. HierarchicalLanguageModel describes multilevel language representations rather than uniquely identifying a word-probability tree. ImplicitLanguageModel and EnergyBasedLLM score whole sequences without autoregressive factorization, unlike LBL’s conditional energy. FactoredLanguageModel denotes explicit linguistic factors; FactorizedLLM denotes component/expert decomposition. DeepFeedForwardNetwork inherits the multiple-hidden-layer requirement, while the named constructions do not require that depth; Perceptron is a binary linear classifier. EmbeddingLayer, OutputLayer, SoftmaxLayer, HiddenLayer and ProbabilisticHiddenLayer are components, not equivalent complete architectures. BayesianNetwork provides a broader factorization viewpoint but not these parameterizations. RBM/Boltzmann identities require stochastic undirected structure absent here. HierarchicalSoftmax is an output component; DocNADE has additive order-insensitive prefix features, NADE binary fully visible conditionals, and ReplicatedSoftmax undirected length-conditioned latent structure. These older records are boundary context, not newly approved targets.
